title: The American V-Twin Cruiser That Brings The Thump, Heritage, and Character Of A True Classic - Top Speed
content: For more than a century, the American V-twin has written the rules of cruising, with a thumping idle, low-rev torque, and big cylinders on display. Lately, though, the segment has started chasing spec sheets instead of soul. Liquid-cooled heads, sophisticated rider aids, and digital displays are increasingly common. None of that is bad engineering, and plenty of riders welcome it. Still, some old-school riders look for a more mechanical kind of honesty, with air-cooled cylinders, deep fenders, and genuine heritage design. In today’s market, that combination has become harder to find. Luckily, one American V-twin cruiser motorcycle still delivers all of it, and it costs less than its looks suggest. Across the cruiser world, the idea of a big, laid-back motorcycle keeps being redrawn. Honda’s Rebel 1100 offers an automatic dual-clutch gearbox, Triumph builds its Rocket 3 around a 2.5-liter triple, and Ducati’s XDiavel V4 pairs a relaxed riding position with sportbike-level power. Each is impressive in its own way, yet together they show how far the class has drifted from the traditional cruiser definition. That shift has made American V-twins the natural refuge for riders who still want the old cruiser feel. Harley-Davidson’s Softail family keeps the air- and oil-cooled Milwaukee-Eight 117 in models like the Heritage Classic and the revived Super Glide, while Indian’s Springfield stays loyal to the air-cooled Thunderstroke 116. Of all these holdouts, though, one goes further than simply keeping the old formula alive, and that makes it a veteran rider’s go-to choice. That motorcycle is Indian’s Chief Vintage, and it wears its history proudly. It draws its inspiration directly from Indian’s 1940s cruisers, and you can see it in the big valanced fenders, the wire wheels, and the floating solo seat. The nostalgia goes deeper than the bodywork, though. Power comes from an air-cooled Thunderstroke 116, the kind of big, unhurried twin that would rather pull than rev. And yes, there’s a touchscreen in the cockpit, but it simply adds a modern touch to what is otherwise a thoroughly traditional package. The Indian Chief Vintage starts at an MSRP of $19,999, but that’s for the black one. Indian’s signature retro red pushes the price a little higher, to $20,499. That isn’t exactly cheap, but the nostalgia and character on offer make it worth the money. For that price, you get wire wheels, floorboards, the illuminated headdress, and silver engine finishes as standard. Our first ride review found the bike strikes a fine balance between value and premium retro looks. As a commemorative model in the Chief lineup celebrating its 100th anniversary, the Chief Vintage is already all about nostalgia. But for riders who want even more of it, Indian offers two special edition models that take this celebration a step (or two) further. Enter the Chief Vintage 125th Anniversary Edition and the Sturgis, SD Edition, which start at $24,999 and $23,999, respectively. Granted, Indian Motorcycle is asking a pretty penny for what is essentially just an exclusive paint scheme. However, if you’re a collector or an Indian Motorcycle enthusiast, that premium will be well worth considering. Not to forget, you’re not only getting an exclusive livery that few modern Indian models wear but a bike that’s genuinely limited-edition and numbered. At the heart of the Chief Vintage sits Indian’s air-cooled Thunderstroke 116. The 1,890cc V-twin uses a long-stroke layout and delivers its peak of 120 lb-ft of torque at just 2,900 rpm. That number says a lot about how it rides. The pull arrives almost the moment you crack the throttle, so overtaking rarely calls for a downshift and a handful of revs. It’s a lazy, muscular kind of performance, and exactly what this style of cruiser demands. The six-speed gearbox pairs with an assist clutch and a belt final drive, which keeps things clean, quiet, and free of chain maintenance. The Chief Vintage takes its cues from the 1940 Chief, widely seen as one of the prettiest motorcycles Indian ever built, and the company didn’t take the task lightly. Its designers worked straight from an older Chief to get the bodywork right. The low-slung fly line, the floating solo saddle, and the vintage handlebars all sell the period look, while the deep-valanced fenders steal the show. The front one carries the illuminated headdress, an Indian hallmark since 1947, with wire wheels peeking out below. Even the engine plays along. Its black cylinders keep non-machined fins, and the heads and pushrod tubes are painted silver to echo the aluminum heads of early Chiefs. It’s a modern motor in period dress, and it sits proudly on display. Park the Vintage beside the original Chief, and you’d swear they came from the same era. Underneath, the Chief Vintage shares its steel-tube frame with the rest of the Chief family, paired with a narrow cast-aluminum rear subframe. Up front, a 46mm fork offers 5.2 inches of travel, while twin preload-adjustable shocks tucked low at the rear provide 3.0 inches. It’s a simple, traditional setup, tuned for comfort over sharp handling. With a 64-inch wheelbase and a 721-pound wet weight, the Chief Vintage prioritizes stability over agility, staying calm and planted on the highway. A 27-inch seat height keeps your feet flat on the ground at stops, while mini-ape bars on a 3-inch riser and wide floorboards set you upright and relaxed for the long haul. Braking comes from a single 298mm floating disc at each end, gripped by a four-piston caliper up front and a two-piston caliper at the rear. The Chief Vintage may look retro, but its feature list is firmly modern. The highlight is a 4-inch round TFT display running Indian’s Ride Command system. Alongside the usual readouts, it handles navigation, Bluetooth connectivity, and ride data, and it can be paired with an optional Bluetooth speaker. The lighting is all-LED, and keyless ignition, cruise control, and USB and 12-volt charging ports come standard. The ride-by-wire throttle offers three modes, Tour, Standard, and Sport, and the rear cylinder shuts down at a standstill to keep heat off your legs in traffic. There’s no six-axis IMU, though. The Chief Vintage isn’t the only way to buy into nostalgia. Harley-Davidson’s Heritage Classic also starts at $19,999 and pairs its air- and oil-cooled Milwaukee-Eight 117 with lockable saddlebags, making it the more road-trip-ready choice straight out of the showroom. The Fat Boy, from $22,599, goes for chrome-heavy swagger inspired by its 1990s original. Look beyond America, and BMW’s R 18 delivers a similar sense of occasion with its huge boxer twin and styling borrowed from the brand’s 1930s machines. Picking between them comes down to taste, and none is a wrong answer. But if the cruiser world has been chasing spec sheets instead of soul, the Chief Vintage is one of the few heading the other way. It was never built to chase numbers. It’s built to feel right the moment that big air-cooled twin settles into its lazy idle, and for the right rider, that matters more than anything else. title: Cadillac’s $239K Escalade-V Collector Series Is Numbered by Year, 1902 to 2027, and Only 252 Will Be Built - Yahoo Autos
content: Most limited editions hand you a number on a plaque. Cadillac's anniversary Escalade-V hands you a year from the company's own history, and you get to pick which one. Cadillac revealed the Escalade-V Collector Series on Oct. 22 in Austin, timed to the U.S. Grand Prix weekend. It's the first Escalade admitted to the Collector Series, the limited-run program Cadillac started in 2022. Only 252 will be built, they're for the U.S. and Canada only, and orders are already open. The number 252 looks arbitrary until you do the math. Cadillac offers two paints, Midnight Stone Frost and Vibrant White Tricoat, and each color gets trucks labeled 1902 through 2027. Count that span inclusively and you get 126 years, not 125. Double it for the two colors and you have 252. So every serial exists exactly twice, once dark and once white. If "1959" is your tailfin-era dream number, you're sharing it with one stranger. Pricing starts at approximately $239,000 with destination, before tax, title and dealer fees. Cadillac also notes that the dealer sets the final price, which is a polite way of saying the sticker is a starting point. For context, Cadillac's Escalade-V page lists the regular 2027 truck from $169,300. That puts the gap at roughly $70,000, depending on how destination is counted. VW Lost the Scout Direct-Sales Fight Over the Word "Affiliate," Asked a California Judge for a Do-Over, and Got a Firm No A Missouri Suburb Allegedly Towed 150+ Cars From Driveways and Backyards With No Warrant or Hearing. Now It's Getting Sued None of that money buys horsepower. The release lists no powertrain changes, so expect the same hand-built 6.2-liter supercharged V8 rated at 682 horsepower and 653 lb-ft. Here's where the premium goes: Carbon-fiber grille surround, lower rear fascia, mirror caps and engine cover Blue brake calipers, dark-finish badges and heritage V-8 puddle lamps Black and Sheer Gray cabin with Santorini Blue stitching and blue seat belts Illuminated sill plates, exclusive badging, special floor mats and a blue key fob The blue has a backstory. Cadillac says Santorini Blue came from the V-Series emblem, debuted on the Project GTP concept and later showed up on the Le Monstre and Petit Pataud Collector Series cars. The Escalade is the first SUV to wear it as the signature accent. Cadillac says buyers can select their VIN along with the serial number. Most of a VIN is fixed by federal rule, not by taste. Under 49 CFR 565.15, position 9 is a check digit produced by a formula, position 10 is the model-year code ("V" for 2027), and position 11 identifies the assembly plant. For high-volume manufacturers like GM, positions 12 through 17 must be the sequentially assigned production number. So nobody is getting "CADDY1902" stamped under the windshield. What Cadillac can offer is a reserved slot in the production sequence, and it hasn't said exactly which characters buyers control. If a specific VIN matters to you, get it in writing on the order before you hand over a deposit. Insurance: Standard policies usually pay actual cash value, and that figure is built from comparable sales. With 252 trucks and no resale history yet, there are no comparables. Anyone buying this as a keeper should look into an agreed-value policy before delivery. Keep the window sticker, order confirmation and build documentation. They're the provenance file. All It Took to Get Into Florida's Driver Records Was One Plant City Police Login on a Personal Device, State Says Rack Up 16 School-Zone Camera Tickets in a Year and NYC Can Put a Speed Limiter on Your Car Starting in 2027 Repairs: Mechanically this is an Escalade-V, so routine service and powertrain parts are ordinary GM business. The edition-specific pieces are a different story. One-off forged 24s and carbon exterior trim won't be sitting on dealer shelves. A curbed wheel or a cracked carbon fascia could mean special-order waits and real money. Market: Because dealers set the final price, early allocations will probably come with markups. Long term, our guess is that values will hinge on the serial number more than the color. Bookend years like 1902 and 2027, plus years tied to famous Cadillacs, should outrun the anonymous mid-century numbers. Treat that as informed speculation, not a forecast. Cadillac wants roughly $70,000 more for a truck whose release lists no powertrain changes, and the release doesn't claim otherwise. What you're buying is scarcity, and the scarcity is a counting exercise: 126 years, two paints. If 1949 in Midnight Stone Frost is your number, you already know. title: Coventry City v Sunderland: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Bottom two sides Coventry and Sunderland meet on Saturday (15:00 GMT) both looking to climb away from the danger zone. Coventry scored 97 goals in last season's Championship, which was at least 15 more than any other team, but they've struggled for goals since coming up to the top flight. They have scored a joint-division-low six goals and have failed to score in five of their eight Premier League games so far this season, more than any other team. Four of those six goals came in one match (their 4-1 win over Newcastle) The Sky Blues also have the lowest xG (7.65) and the lowest open play xG so far in this campaign (4.78), with just 25 shots on target, the second-worst in the division after Aston Villa. Their xG in last weekend's draw at home to fellow strugglers Fulham was 0.51, which was their lowest since their opening game of the season, which was away at champions Arsenal. Coventry are the only team in the Premier League this season to neither win any points from losing positions nor drop any points when leading – in their eight matches, the team scoring first has won every time. That's further bad news for Sky Blues fans, whose team have failed to score in the first half in seven of their eight league games this season. Like Coventry, Sunderland have scored a joint-division low of six goals in this season's Premier League. At the same stage in 2025-26, the Black Cats had only scored three more times, but the crucial difference is that they had 14 points, as opposed to the five they have earned in 2026-27. It's the biggest drop-off after eight games of any Premier League team. Head coach Regis Le Bris has talked of "embracing" Sunderland's busy schedule of playing in Europe and in the Carabao Cup but their Premier League form does appear to be paying the price. The Black Cats earned four points in their first three league games of the season, all of which preceded the start of their EFL Cup and Europa League campaigns. Since those began, they have picked up just one point, losing four out of five games. Conversely, they have won four out of their five games in the cup competitions, reaching the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday with their 3-2 victory over Brentford. That means they will have another midweek fixture to add to what looks like being a busy pre-Christmas period for Le Bris's side.

title: Advocate General Opinion in ByteDance v Commission: A Look at the DMA Gatekeeper Rebuttal Mechanism - Cleary Antitrust Watch

Learn more about cookies. On October 15, 2026, the Advocate General’s opinion was delivered in ByteDance’s appeal to the Court of Justice against the General Court’s 2024 judgment upholding the Commission’s decision to designate it as a gatekeeper under the DMA for its TikTok core platform service. This is the first DMA case to reach the Court of Justice. The Advocate General’s opinion is meant to guide the Court’s decision-making but is not binding. The judgment is expected at a later date. In summary, the Advocate General held that the standard of proof is high for undertakings meeting the quantitative thresholds to call into question the presumptions. The undertaking must show with a “high degree of plausibility” that it does not meet the qualitative criteria set out in Art 3(2) DMA. The arguments set out for this purpose must be “genuinely compelling, with no easily identifiable weaknesses in their capacity to rebut the presumption”. The Opinion holds that ByteDance was unable to demonstrate any manifest errors in the General Court’s finding that ByteDance did not discharge this burden. According to the Advocate General, the evidence ByteDance adduced in its rebuttal case was insufficiently substantiated to warrant outright non-designation or the opening of a market investigation. The Commission designated ByteDance as a gatekeeper for TikTok in September 2023, finding that ByteDance met the DMA’s quantitative thresholds and that its rebuttal arguments (including reliance on limited EU turnover) were not sufficiently substantiated to manifestly call those presumptions into question. The General Court dismissed ByteDance’s annulment action in July 2024. While it helpfully confirmed that the types of evidence a presumed gatekeeper can adduce to contest designation include qualitative evidence and are not limited to quantitative data, it imposed a very high burden of proof. It indicated that this burden cannot be discharge by presenting “doubts” or “prima facie” evidence, but that the arguments put forward must be sufficiently substantiated to manifestly call into question the presumption. On this basis it ruled that the evidence ByteDance put forward during the administrative proceedings was insufficient: While the Opinion is not binding, it may foreshadow that a high standard for the purpose of rebutting the gatekeeper presumption will be endorsed by the Court. Regardless of the exact standard eventually found by the Court of Justice, it will remain crucial for presumed gatekeepers to present rebuttal arguments during the administrative phase that are sufficiently compelling, well substantiated and concrete. While it is encouraging that the Advocate General confirmed the Commission must engage in a case-by-case assessment and take account of different types of evidence, the burden is on the presumed gatekeeper to determine which evidence is most relevant. The ByteDance experience shows that presumed gatekeepers cannot necessarily count on a genuine steer or dialogue with the Commission in this regard. This would be exacerbated if the Commission were to scrap its practice of communicating its preliminary findings in advance of designation (if the Court confirms, in line with the Opinion, that it is not required to do so). All this reinforces the importance for presumed gatekeepers of building a thorough and well-evidenced record for their engagement with the Commission, particularly where they wish to raise arguments around comparative size compared to other players, multi-homing, lack of an ecosystem, lack of network effects or user lock-in, business dependency, and geographic origin of scale and turnover.

title: Brentford v Nottingham Forest: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Brentford will attempt to earn their third win of the season, against a Nottingham Forest side who go into the weekend in the bottom three in the table. BBC Sport examines some of the key themes ahead of Saturday's meeting at Gtech Community Stadium (15:00 GMT). In last weekend's draw against Hull City, Brentford conceded first for the first time in all competitions this season. It happened again against Sunderland in the EFL Cup in midweek, where they let in three goals in a 13-minute first-half spell. Although ultimately fruitless, the Bees did at least fight back with two goals, one of which came in injury time from Igor Thiago, who will be hoping that can spark some league form. The Brazil international scored 22 league goals in 2025-26, but he's managed just one in eight games so far this season despite an expected goals total of 3.79. Luckily for him, his team-mates have been finding the net, with Brentford the only side other than leaders Manchester City to have scored in all eight of their Premier League games so far this season. Jaidon Anthony has only contributed one but does have a good record against Nottingham Forest, scoring three goals in four Premier League appearances against them for Bournemouth and Burnley. Two of those games ended in draws, which is something Brentford are making a habit of, having drawn five of their eight league matches this season. At first glance, Nottingham Forest are in a similar position to last season. After eight games they have one more point (six to five in 2025-26) in 18th. It was at this stage last season that Forest sacked their manager for the second time in the campaign, so current boss Oliver Glasner must be feeling a bit nervous. But Glasner also had a slow start at former club Crystal Palace. He didn't win any of his opening six games in charge and the Eagles also didn't win any of their first eight in his first full season. And while the results are similar to last season, the performances are more encouraging. As the Austrian has pointed out, Forest are creating opportunities. They are third in the Premier League for shots taken (137) and fifth for big chances created (19). His side are sixth in the expected goals table (13.49) but joint-bottom when it comes to real goals (6). That xG underperformance comes out at -7.49, the biggest shortfall in the Premier League by some margin – a gap that was increased in the 1-1 draw against Ipswich last time out, when Forest had 17 shots and an xG of 2.29. Glasner believes it's only a matter of time before the chances turn into goals, but Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is notoriously impatient where results are concerned, as four managers last season can confirm.

title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Liverpool welcome Arsenal to Anfield on Sunday (16:30 GMT) in a heavyweight Premier League tussle. After losing 3-0 to Manchester City, Liverpool have won four games in succession and are now six points off the top. They won at home in the league for the first time since April on Sunday, against Brighton, and carry the momentum of a Carabao Cup victory over Chelsea - 6-5 on penalties after a 1-1 draw - into Sunday's huge game. As for Arsenal, they will hope their EFL Cup exit to fourth-tier Fleetwood Town does not distract from the defence of their title. The Gunners coasted past Everton last weekend to move level on points with Manchester City, who had earlier slipped up at Aston Villa. They do have a dreadful record at Anfield, though, and Mikel Arteta will be looking to put that right. Liverpool are starting to build momentum under new head coach Andoni Iraola and will be quietly confident of staying in contention for the Premier League title. Crucially, some of the club's big-money signings have started to hit form, most notably star forward Alexander Isak. The striker now has six goals in the Premier League this season – a tally bettered only by Erling Haaland – and has scored in his past three matches in the top flight. His game has become much more focused on penalty-box play this term, and he has showcased a ruthless streak with the opportunities he has had which is comparable to the Manchester City striker. Liverpool have also loved welcoming Arsenal to Anfield down the years. In the past 13 Premier League meetings on Merseyside, the home side have won eight and drawn five. The Gunners' last top-flight victory there came in 2012 through goals from Lukas Podolski and Santi Cazorla. Arsenal will be looking to put that shock loss to Fleetwood behind them quickly. Arteta would have been content with what he saw in the 2-0 win over Everton last weekend, especially following a draining 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich three days earlier. The win over the Toffees felt a lot more like the Arsenal of last season. The Gunners scored their first after seven minutes and, in doing so, registered their first non-penalty set-piece goal in the Premier League this season. They also didn't give their opponents a sniff of goal. Centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel grabbed the goals. At the back, the pair have been forming a solid partnership, with the team showing familiar defensive bite over their past two Premier League games to keep two clean sheets. Aside from a ropey display on the road at Brighton, where they lost 3-0, the Gunners have once again been the standard-setters at the back. They have the best defensive record in the division for goals conceded, while their underlying numbers are also the most impressive in the league after eight games.

title: Manchester City v Brighton & Hove Albion: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Top-flight leaders Manchester City were given an almighty scare at home by third-placed Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday but they have won their past 10 league games on Halloween. After making a combined 16 changes to their starting line-ups in midweek, which City won on penalties, both sides will be back to full strength for Saturday's rematch in the league (15:00 GMT). Moving on from Pep Guardiola was never likely to be easy for Manchester City but their status as league leaders and Carabao Cup quarter-finalists shows they remain an excellent side. Nonetheless, City's 100% winning league record this season was ended by Aston Villa last Saturday and they were rattled by visitors Brighton in midweek before winning a penalty shootout. One weakness of Enzo Maresca's City is that they can be open in midfield and invite pressure. They have faced nine shots from counter-attacks across their past five games in all competitions, compared to five in their first nine fixtures. While just one counter-attack has led to a goal, City have followed a run of five clean sheets in six matches by conceding 11 times in five subsequent outings. Only five teams in Europe's five biggest leagues have a worse recent defensive record in all competitions over that period. Brighton head coach Fabian Hürzeler felt Manchester City "had the luck" during Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie, adding: "We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge." He has elected to keep his squad in the north-west in-between successive visits to the Etihad Stadium, which come amid a sequence of five away matches in a row. Brighton are winless from the first three, each in a different competition. Albion, though, remain the league's top scorers and a point this weekend would give them their highest tally after nine games of a top-flight season. They are unbeaten in four league matches against Manchester City, including back-to-back draws at the Etihad, but have never won away in this fixture in 16 attempts. It's the most times Brighton have faced a league opponent away without ever winning, as well as being Manchester City's longest unbeaten home record against a team without ever losing.

title: Aston Villa v Fulham: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Aston Villa and Fulham were knocked out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but will both be seeking a third consecutive league win on Saturday night (20:00 GMT). The hosts have a strong home record in this fixture, with their solitary defeat in 18 Premier League meetings at Villa Park coming in April 2014. Aston Villa are yet to lose a Premier League game in the month of October under Unai Emery, winning eight times and drawing four. Last Saturday's win over league leaders Manchester City marked the four-year anniversary of Emery's appointment, and on Friday this week he surpassed Martin O'Neill as the club's longest-serving manager since the gilded reign of Ron Saunders from 1974 to 1982. After admitting he used the difficult first month of the campaign before the international break as an extended pre-season to mould his new-look side, Emery's Villa 2.0 are taking shape. The club's two most expensive signings are more than justifying their hefty price tags, with Johan Manzambi a creative tour de force and Nicolas Jackson scoring six goals in as many games. Villa reeled off six wins and a draw in seven games across all competitions before Wednesday's limp surrender by mostly fringe players at Bournemouth in a customary early Carabao Cup exit under the Spaniard. "Premier League is the priority," said an unapologetic Emery afterwards. That being the case, Villa have been meeting their manager's demands of late, earning a league-high 10 points from the past four rounds of matches. While Villa are in thrall to their Spanish manager, many Fulham supporters are reserving judgement on theirs. Some of the pressure on Alvaro Arbeloa was alleviated by consecutive 1-0 league wins over promoted opponents, but Wednesday's Carabao Cup defeat at home to struggling Crystal Palace has stirred up the unrest. That tie was an all-too-familiar tale under Arbeloa of dominating possession but lacking a cutting edge. Fulham average 58% possession in the league this season – the fifth highest – and can be easy on the eye; only Manchester City have strung together more sequences of at least 10 passes, and no side can match Fulham for the volume of those ending in a touch or shot in the opposition penalty area. There's no lack of effort either, with Arsenal the only side to cover more ground this season. Having improved defensively of late, Fulham's major ongoing issue is that they're not taking their chances. The Cottagers rank in the league's top 10 for a variety of attacking metrics – including more goal attempts on target than Arsenal – but their shot conversion rate is the fourth worst in the division.

title: 2026-2027 Audree V. Fowler Fellows in Protein Science - UCLA – Chemistry and Biochemistry
content:
Graduate students Lenka Milojević (Zhou group), Akshaya Narayanasamy (Lindert group), Sarah Singleton (Conway group), and Janet Zhong (Feigon group) have been selected as 2026–27 Fowler Fellows and shared their research at a special event on Oct. 13, 2026. About the 2026-27 Audree Fowler Fellows in Protein Science Lenka Milojević is a fifth-year Biophysics Ph.D. candidate in the lab of Professor Z. Hong Zhou at UCLA. As an undergraduate at Maastricht University, she studied the structural basis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis virulence and amyloid-β fibril nucleation in the lab of Professor Peter Peters. She completed her bachelor’s thesis research at UCLA in the lab of Professor David Eisenberg, focusing on amyloid disaggregation, before beginning her doctoral studies. In the Zhou lab, Lenka uses cryo-electron tomography to visualize and characterize membrane-associated protein assemblies across a range of viral and cellular systems. Akshaya Narayanasamy is a fifth-year Ph.D. student in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at UCLA, mentored by Professor Steffen Lindert. She earned her B.S.-M.S. in Chemistry from the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram, where she worked in Professor Mahesh Hariharan’s lab investigating how single-atom substitutions influence crystal packing and charge transport behavior. She received her M.S. in Physical Chemistry from The Ohio State University before moving with the Lindert lab to UCLA. At UCLA, Akshaya develops integrative modeling methods that combine deep learning and Rosetta with experimental data, such as ion mobility mass spectrometry and cryo-EM, to improve protein structure prediction. Her current work focuses on developing an experimentally guided diffusion model and designing de novo protein binders with potential antibacterial activity. Ultimately, she aims to bridge AI-based structure prediction and experimental data to make computational protein models more reliable for drug discovery and therapeutic design. Sarah Singleton is a fourth-year BMSB student, working in Professor Stuart Conway’s lab. She earned her B.S. in Biochemistry at Simmons University (Fenway, MA). Her research is centered on drugging the previously undruggable class of proteins—transcription factors. Zinc finger (ZF)-containing transcription factor proteins typically contain multiple ZF motifs, but little is known about the principles that govern the recognition of multi-ZF arrays by immunomodulatory imide drugs (IMiDs). In a multi-ZF array that contains several potentially targetable ZFs, which will be accessible and why? How does the surrounding protein architecture inform IMiD recognition? Sarah’s research aims to utilize her findings on the fundamental principles of ZF recognition to design IMiD therapeutics for transcription factors involved in health and disease. Janet Zhong is a fourth-year BMSB student, working in Professor Juli Feigon’s laboratory. She received her B.Sc. and M.Res. from Imperial College London. At UCLA, Janet combines cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical approaches to investigate how proteins and RNAs assemble into ribonucleoprotein structures. Her research focuses on telomerase, the enzyme that maintains chromosome ends, with interests in its structure, assembly, and mechanisms. She has also worked on capturing the cryo-EM structure of a small bacterial non-coding RNA called raiA motif RNA. A strong supporter of the basic sciences and medicine at UCLA, alumna Dr. Audree Fowler (B.S. ’56 chemistry, Ph.D. ’63 biochemistry) established the Audree V. Fowler Fellows in Protein Science in 2008. Fowler was Director of the UCLA Protein Microsequencing Facility from 1984-1999 and is a Researcher Emeritus of the UCLA Department of Biological Chemistry. She is one of the first four women to receive a Ph.D. from the UCLA Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry. In 2018, the women were awarded the department’s 2018 Alumni Legacy Awards in recognition of their achievements in life, and generous support and service to UCLA. “The sciences gave me a great life. Now I want to help others have access to the same opportunities I enjoyed,” Fowler explained when she established the Fowler Fellowships endowment. Applications for the fellowships are solicited from graduate students in the Molecular Biology Interdepartmental (MBI) Ph.D. Program, Biological Chemistry, and Chemistry & Biochemistry Departments. In addition to presenting their research at a special seminar, the recipients each receive a $5,000 award. title: Manchester United v Roma: Svilar unlikely to be fit for the game at Old Trafford - Yahoo Sports
content: As reported by SportMediaset, Roma goalkeeper Mile Svilar will not be fit for the Manchester United game and is set to remain sidelined for a while longer. Svilar, who's out with a broken toe since the start of the month, was anticipating an early return, but Roma are taking no chances and have decided to prolong his recovery phase through the imminent international break. Pierluigi Gollini, who has been deputising for Svilar, is expected to be between the sticks for the game at Old Trafford. Despite going with their No. 2 on the pitch, the Giallorossi won't be too worried about their chances in their latest Champions League encounter. The mood in and around Manchester United is, to put it simply, funereal, with any sense of form and belief nonexistent. Roma have been conceding goals of late, and they must still be ruing that defeat to Real Madrid, but they should be able to get a win here and march forwards towards knockout qualification. Roma's other two games before the international break are in Serie A: a trip to Udinese followed by a home game against Sassuolo after the trio to Manchester.

title: Hearts & Hibs brace for 'all or nothing' semi-final - BBC
content: Wouter Vrancken and Marink Reedijk both managed in Belgium last season On Sunday, fans of Hearts and Hibernian will make the same journey to Hampden but the Edinburgh rivals have been on different paths so far this season. Hearts sold out their initial allocation for the Premier Sports Cup semi-final in three days, then snapped up a second wave to take their numbers over 23,000. That a few seats will be empty at the other end of the national stadium signals a degree of trepidation among followers of Hibs. Still, more than 18,000 will be there to cheer on the team sitting second bottom of the Premiership, having taken a mere two points from their past eight outings. Hearts lie third and enjoyed their third successive derby victory in early September. Hearts can also boast a 100% record in derbies played at Hampden, all coming in the Scottish Cup. The teams have been going at it since Christmas Day 1875 but had to wait until 2006 for a first meeting in Glasgow's Southside. Paul Hartley scored a hat-trick in a 4-0 semi-final triumph, while Hibs had two players sent off. Then came the 2012 final, a 5-1 demolition, with a double from Rudi Skacel and a red card for the losers. The past two contests were closer, Hearts prevailing 2-1 each time in the semi-finals of 2020 and 2022, with yet another Hibs dismissal in the latter to go with the pain of a missed penalty in the former. Live commentary on BBC Radio Scotland, follow the action on BBC Sport app and website. Reedijk denied first Hibs win by late St Mirren leveller This is a first competitive match between managers that were on track to meet in the Belgian top flight this season before stepping away. Wouter Vrancken steered Sint-Truiden to third, their best finish in 60 years, while Marink Reedijk enjoyed a remarkable 'invincibles' second tier title success with Beveren. Reedijk is still waiting for his first Hibs victory, a drab draw at St Mirren on Wednesday following three defeats for the Dutchman who replaced David Gray and has set about implementing a new style at Easter Road. While the structure is evolving, Hibs remain defensively fragile, without a league clean sheet, and have been blunt in attack. In Reedijk's first game, Hibs had four efforts on target, then three, then two, while the goal at St Mirren came from the only one. In their past four domestic outings, Hearts have had 22 attempts on target and that includes a 7-1 mauling at Celtic. Vrancken's side have 24 league goals to Hibs' 11, three of those coming at Easter Road when they completely bossed the first half, showing far greater energy and intensity than the hosts. "You have to put your emotions and energy in the things you have to do on the pitch and go from there," said Vrancken. "We did really well there and we have to do also on Sunday. "It's a totally different game. New manager, new style, new competition. It's also an all-or-nothing game. So all different circumstances. The first game doesn't matter anymore. We have to look forward to this one." Meanwhile, Reedijk is looking forward to a "special match" with "some surprises somewhere", adding: "It's not only the derby, it's also a semi-final, and it's one step away from a final, so that is a double way of excitement." Having come so close in the title race last season, some silverware would go a long way to underline Hearts' credentials as disruptors of the established order. The Tynecastle side haven't lifted a trophy since their colossal party in 2012 and last got their hands on the League Cup in 1962. Hibs have won the competition three times in that time. Both teams have long injury lists, but the return of the experienced Martin Boyle, scorer of five derby goals, is a boost for Hibs. The 33-year-old lit up the 2021 semi-finals with a first-half hat-trick in a win over Rangers. Boyle has three league goals, making him the club's top scorer. Hearts have five players on three goals or more, Claudio Braga and Calvin Miller both moving on to five in Wednesday's thrilling draw at home to Rangers. After dominating for long spells, Vrancken's men did fade in that game and might have lost at the death if not for a mis-timed jump from Dujon Sterling. Early exits from both cup competitions perhaps benefited Hearts' surprise league challenge last time but, with Conference League group games in the mix this time, the action is coming thick and fast. Can Hibs stay in the game long enough to test that stamina? A foolish sending off killed their momentum in the last derby after pulling a goal back and they certainly cannot afford to add to that list of Hampden red cards. title: A British Marque Is Building a 200-MPH Audi Quattro with a V-8 That Revs to 10,000 RPM - Car and Driver
content:
The Audacious Automotive IV is built on the B7 RS4 and has a claimed top speed of 200 mph. Few cars have as famed a history as the Audi Quattro, and even fewer cars have been reimagined as many times. The newest tribute to Audi’s legendary Quattro is the Audacious Automotive IV. It’s being built by a small British manufacturer whose passion drove it to fit its creation with a V-8 that revs to 10,000 rpm. The IV combines B7-generation Audi RS4 underpinnings with the look—and in some cases, bodywork—of the short-wheelbase Audi Quattro. While the Quattro was famous for its five-cylinder engine, Audacious felt the RS4’s 4.2-liter V-8 was a better fit for its tribute car. Coincidentally enough, the builder says the IV will be offered with four engine configurations. The standard setup takes the 4.2-liter V-8 and adds a supercharger, increasing power to 592 ponies. Strengthened internals and improved cooling from Audacious’ Stage Two conversion bring that figure to 740 hp. Plus, there are supercharged and naturally aspirated options that raise the engine’s redline from an already lofty 8250 to an otherworldly 10,000 rpm. It doesn’t seem like the higher redline offers any additional power, but it should sound the business. Whichever engine customers choose, every IV will use the RS4’s original six-speed manual gearbox. Audacious claims the Quattro recreation will accelerate from zero to 60 mph in 3.4 seconds and reach a top speed of 200 mph, though the brand doesn’t disclose which configuration will reach that terminal velocity. Customers can order their IV with metal bodywork sourced from an original Quattro donor, or they can have their car built from a new carbon-fiber body that doesn’t require any donor car. According to a report from Autocar, the company expects the latter to make up around 80 percent of its orders. The automaker is targeting a curb weight of around 2755 pounds for the carbon versions and around 3140 pounds for the donor cars. Like the original Quattro, the interior has been overhauled to be a bit more raw, though at least in the examples shown, the whole thing is draped in leather. With every car being hand-built, Audacious promises that no two IVs will be exactly the same. Of course, as a coachbuilt model produced by a team the size of Audacious Automotive, production will be extremely limited. It doesn’t hurt that exclusivity sells, and with the IV being limited to just 50 hand-built units worldwide, that number shouldn’t be too hard to hit. There is the price to consider, though, and the IV doesn’t come cheap, with a starting price of roughly $468,650 (based on current exchange rates). Jack Fitzgerald’s love for cars stems from his as yet unshakable addiction to Formula 1. 
After a brief stint as a detailer for a local dealership group in college, he knew he needed a more permanent way to drive all the new cars he couldn’t afford and decided to pursue a career in auto writing. By hounding his college professors at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, he was able to travel Wisconsin seeking out stories in the auto world before landing his dream job at Car and Driver. His new goal is to delay the inevitable demise of his 2010 Volkswagen Golf. title: Alfonso V. Masangkay - Sequim Gazette
content: Dr. Alfonso V. Masangkay, 69, of Sequim, Washington, passed away on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Born on October 30, 1956, Alfonso was the son of Nicolas and Maura Masangkay, both educators who served as his lifelong teachers, not only in the classroom but also in life. He earned his medical degree from the University of Santo Tomas Faculty of Medicine and Surgery in Manila, Philippines. He went on to complete his residency at Metropolitan Hospital Center in New York and a fellowship in surgical pathology at North Shore University Hospital. Alfonso enjoyed a long and distinguished career as a pathologist, during which he served as an inspector for the College of American Pathologists and as Laboratory Medical Director at Olympic Medical Center. He concluded his career with InCyte Diagnostics before retiring in 2024. Above all, Alfonso was a devoted husband and father who worked tirelessly to provide for his family and ensure they were always well cared for. He is survived by his beloved wife of 44 years, Dr. Brenda Masangkay; his three children, Neil Masangkay (Rachel Slotcavage), Nicole Masangkay, and Allison Masangkay; and his brother, Leonardo Masangkay. Outside of his professional life, Alfonso was an avid golfer, enthusiastic cook, and an endless source of dad jokes. He will be fondly remembered for his kindness, generous heart, and wonderful sense of humor. Alfonso will be deeply missed by his family, friends, and all those whose lives he touched. A viewing was held on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, from 3:00 to 8:00 p.m. at Evergreen Washelli Funeral Home, 11111 Aurora Avenue North, Seattle, WA 98133. A Mass of Christian Burial was celebrated on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at Blessed Sacrament Catholic Church, 5050 8th Avenue NE, Seattle, WA 98105. Burial followed at Holyrood Cemetery, 205 NE 205th Street, Shoreline, WA 98155. Arrangements have been entrusted to Evergreen Washelli Funeral Home in Seattle, Washington. title: Honda CR-V vs. Hyundai Tucson vs. Nissan Rogue: Owners Have Spoken - Autoblog
content: BMW Alpina's First New Model Spied as a V8-Powered 7 Series Toyota Unveils Five Rugged Woodland Concepts, Including A Lifted Sienna Arizona Trooper Stops Hoodless Camaro at 105 MPH, Finds Bigger Problem Which of these popular compact SUVs delivers what it promises? One impresses out of the box, while another is the better long term buy. Best Subcompact SUVs For 2027: Our 5 Picks From $21,700 A Good Friend's Tesla Model S Lease is Ending. Here's What I Told Him to Get as a Replacement Best Sports Cars For 2027: Affordable Fun to 1,250 HP Compact SUVs are among the most popular vehicles on sale. Some of the top sellers include models like the Honda CR-V, Hyundai Tucson, and Nissan Rogue. All three endeavor to deliver the best comfort, practicality and overall reliability in this hard-fought segment. The Honda CR-V entered its sixth generation for the 2023 model year, bringing more standard active safety tech, and an updated two-motor hybrid setup. The Hyundai Tucson arrived in its radical fourth-generation form in 2022, debuting a somewhat divisive angular origami styling, but also packed with tech and features like expansive digital screens, and plenty of drivetrain options. It is due for imminent replacement, but the current model remains a popular buy. The Nissan Rogue arrived in 2021 and has been continually updated and refined with tech like a variable-compression turbocharged engine, bolder styling and dual digital displays. But which one of these compact SUVs scores the highest in terms of owner satisfaction? We decided to find out by comparing them using survey data from J.D. Power and Kelley Blue Book (KBB). J.D. Power calculates scores focusing on the first 90 days of ownership for initial quality/design and three years for long-term dependability. Kelley Blue Book gets its consumer ratings data from constant owner feedback over a vehicle’s entire production run. Examining both of these results provides a good insight into just how well these vehicles perform from initial impressions to long term real-world use. Owner satisfaction surveys provide an overall view of a vehicle’s performance in real-world scenarios. They cover everything from the, fuel efficiency, ride comfort, driving experience and build quality to long-term reliability and the dealership experience. The Honda CR-V uses a 190-hp 1.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder paired with a continuously variable transmission (CVT), while upper trims feature a 204-hp two-motor hybrid system. Front-wheel drive (FWD) is standard, while all-wheel drive (AWD) is optional or standard on higher trims. The sixth-generation CR-V offers a high-quality user-friendly cabin layout, great fuel economy, and segment-leading cargo flexibility. The Hyundai Tucson kicks off with a naturally aspirated 187-hp 2.5-liter inline-four and an eight-speed automatic transmission. It is also offered with 226-hp hybrid and 261-hp plug-in hybrid powertrains as well. It offers quiet cruising characteristics, generous warranty coverage, a high-tech cockpit, and a more subdued exterior design since 2025. The Nissan Rogue has been around the longest, but it still offers solid value, a lot of standard and optional features, as well as a very comfortable interior and decent fuel economy. Let’s see whether the owners think of their vehicles. J.D. Power surveys encompassing the past five model years show strong initial customer satisfaction scores across the board, aside from the first year of the new generation Tucson, which pulled its overall average down. Both the Rogue and CR-V averaged scores within the “Great” tier (81–90). The Nissan Rogue leading this trio with owners impressed by the initial driving experience, interior storage design, and high perceived value on mid-tier SV and Platinum trims. The Honda CR-V saw a mild dip in 2023 during its transition to the sixth generation model, before climbing back up again, and it was noted for its quality, resale value, and interior ergonomic ratings. The Tucson posted slightly lower quality and reliability scores in 2022 and 2023, with customers not initially pleased with the touch-panel controls and modest base-engine performance. However, the overall satisfaction score has steadily risen, especially since the 2025 refresh and improved electronic reliability. Kelley Blue Book looks at a longer timeframe than J.D. Power, and it scores vehicles based on owner feedback in categories including performance, styling, comfort, value, and reliability. In a reversal of positions, the Hyundai Tucson holds a commanding lead here, owners commenting positively on the refined and quiet cabin, generous rear passenger space, and impressive hybrid engines. The Honda CR-V maintained its second place, but the results aren’t great, especially after the model change in 2023. While owners praised its ride, cargo volume, and fuel efficiency, negative reviews frequently highlight feature lower spec levels on certain trims and hypersensitive parking assistance systems. The Nissan Rogue drops to third here, getting a consistent but relatively poor 3.6 across the past five model years. Owners had good things to say about the Zero Gravity front seats, exterior looks, and practical cabin layout, but issues with the CVT transmission and reliability concerns over the turbocharged engine kept the satisfaction levels down. Satisfaction surveys if this type tend to include a broad array of objective and subjective metrics, and real-world experiences can vary significantly between owners. While we are comparing the owner satisfaction levels here across three compact SUV rivals, the results don’t indicate which vehicle is the superior choice, rather which one has met the expectations of its owners better. Autoblog brings you car news; expert reviews and exciting pictures and video. Research and compare vehicles, too. A top-spec Hyundai Tucson Plug-In Hybrid needs to may be quicker, more efficient and more luxurious than the base 2.5-liter model, and it will be marked down by owners if it is not. This takes objective stats and imbues them with a subjective, personal quality that gives these surveys a more relatable quality. And judging from these results, a Nissan Rogue or Honda CR-V tend to leave a more favorable impression on owners in the early days of ownership, but if you intend to keep your SUV for more than just a couple of years, then the Hyundai Tucson has them both beat. © 2026 Paradium.AI Autoblog is a registered trademark of Paradium.AI

title: D.C. Memo: Is Flanagan v. Tafoya close, or not? - MinnPost
content:
Nonprofit, independent journalism. Supported by readers. D.C. Memo | A recap of a week’s worth of Washington political news, journalism, and opinion, delivered with an eye toward what matters for Minnesota. WASHINGTON – Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, who was in an unexpectedly close race with Michele Tafoya for retiring Sen. Tina Smith’s seat, may have surged ahead of her rival in the days before next week’s election. A New York Times/Siena poll released Wednesday showed that respondents favored the Democrat Flanagan over former sportscaster Tafoya 54% to 40%. The poll also showed Sen. Amy Klobuchar running far ahead of her Republican rival in the governor’s race, state House Speaker Lisa Demuth, 56% to 38%. The poll said Flanagan’s wide lead comes from many demographics and that she has pulled ahead of Tafoya among both younger and older voters, white and non-white voters and those who are college educated and those who are not. Flanagan also led Tafoya on a number of issues, including the cost of living and foreign wars and even immigration, an issue that typically favors Republicans. Yet the poll also showed Tafoya’s efforts to tie Flanagan to fraud may have caused some damage to the lieutenant governor. Poll respondents ranked concerns about corruption and fraud second only to the economy in terms of issues driving their decisions at the ballot booth. Vice President JD Vance planned to fan the flames of voter concerns of fraud in the state with a trip to St. Cloud on Friday with other members of his “White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.” But the visit to the state was abruptly cancelled just hours after it was announced on Thursday. The White House did not give a reason. The New York Times/Siena poll differed sharply from polls conducted in September and earlier this month that showed Flanagan leading Tafoya by much less and even running neck-and-neck with her rival. In an interview on Fox News, Tafoya called the latest poll “a huge outlier.” There is a chance the New York Time/Siena poll could be inaccurate. It polled a relatively small group of Minnesota voters — only 752 registered voters. It also has a large margin of error, plus-or-minus 3.9% to 4.2%. And the New York Times’ chief political analyst, Nate Cohn, himself cast some doubt on his company’s poll results in Minnesota, saying it may have underestimated Republican strength. “We may look back and say this was the canary in the coal mine — something like a 2026 equivalent of the Selzer poll showing Kamala Harris ahead in neighboring Iowa in 2024,” Cohn wrote. “In hindsight (and even at the time), that result was clearly a warning sign that pollsters were struggling to reach white working-class voters rather than any indication of Democratic strength.” Cohn said Minnesota’s failure to register voters by party makes it difficult for pollsters to get a good read of public sentiment. But he concluded that “the poll may not be as far off as one might usually guess for a big outlier.” “This race might not be a real battleground,” he said. Flanagan may have found some traction in the closing days of the campaign. She has held a rally in Duluth with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and has campaigned with Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn.; Rep. Pramila Jayapal, R-Wash.; and former Transportation Secretary and former Democratic presidential candidate Pete Buttigieg. While Flanagan’s main attack on Tafoya is to link her to President Donald Trump and his policies, Tafoya’s narrative focused on promoting  independence from the president, and even the GOP. Trump has endorsed Tafoya twice, urged Minnesota Republicans to get to the polls to vote for her and insinuated he’d interfere in Minnesota’s election if she is not declared a winner on the evening of Nov. 3. “The only way she can lose is if they cheat by playing games with the ballots as they come in,” he wrote on Truth Social. “We can’t allow that to happen.” Tafoya said she would abide by the results of the election. But the damage may have been done. Nevertheless, the prospect of a close race has prompted the candidates to remove their gloves. Flanagan’s campaign criticized Tafoya for comments made on a podcast she established after she left broadcasting NFL games. In 2023, Tafoya criticized Lisa Guerrero, a former “Monday Night Football” reporter who wrote a memoir describing the sexism she experienced in TV sports and the miscarriage she suffered while reporting a game. Tafoya called Guerrero “an attention seeking drama queen” who “was not tough enough.” Meanwhile, Tafoya took issue about how Flanagan’s wealth grew while working in public office and on a lieutenant governor’s salary of $129,000 a year. According to her financial disclosures, Flanagan and her husband have net worth of between $990,000 and $2.7 million. Flanagan cried foul in a release that said her wealth increased after the death of her mother, who had been the recipient of an inheritance from her aunt. “My mom and Auntie Peggy were two of the most important people in my life,” Flanagan said. “I lost them a year and a half apart, and they left me what they had.” Meanwhile, Tafoya, who is married to Mark Vandersall, a private wealth advisor, reported on her disclosures that she and her husband’s assets were valued between about $17 million and a little more than $33 million. This midterm is the most expensive in history with $11.2 billion spent a week before Election Day, surpassing the 2024 election which included $3.2 billion spent on the presidential race. The costliest Senate race is the more than $500 million spent on the Texas contest between Democratic state Rep. James Talarico and Republican State Attorney General Ken Paxton. The record-breaking spending is a result of a political environment that gives Democrats an opportunity to seize the U.S. Senate from Republican control. To accomplish that, Democrats would have to flip four seats. Yet the race between Flanagan and Tafoya is among the cheapest Senate contests in the nation. According to the Federal Election Commission (FEC), Flanagan had spent about $11 million and Tafoya nearly $9 million on their campaigns as of Oct. 14. Both campaigns have also benefited by about $2 million each worth of help from third parties that have paid for ads and canvassing. The modest spending by outside groups, and the lack of spending by the national parties on the race, is another indication that Minnesota’s U.S. Senate race is not a battleground. ▪️Reporter Claire Carlson wrote that residents of Hastings are fired up about the rising cost of cleaning PFAS in their water. PFAS are a group of highly toxic chemicals used in everyday products like cookware and clothing. ▪️State Government Reporter Matthew Blake took a close look at the surprisingly tight race between Attorney General Keith Ellison and his Republican opponent, Ron Schutz. ▪️Another race that is much closer than expected and could help Democrats take over the U.S. House is playing out in southern Minnesota. That’s where Rep. Brad Finstad, R-1st District, is fending off Democratic challenger Jake Johnson in a race that has attracted millions of dollars from the national parties and other outside groups. ▪️And Metro reporter Trevor Mitchell wrote that juvenile justice is driving the race for Hennepin County attorney. title: Rennes predicted XI v OGC Nice: Brice Samba and Esteban Lepaul out - Yahoo Sports
content: Stade Rennais are without Brice Samba and Esteban Lepaul for their visit to face OGC Nice at the Allianz Riviera on Friday night. The latter is yet to recover from an ankle injury that he sustained against Paris FC earlier this month. Whilst he is nearing his return, it will not come away to Le Gym. He was touch and go to make this game, having missed the draw against Juventus and the win against RC Strasbourg Alsace. Rennes are also without first-choice goalkeeper Samba. In his absence, it is Nicolas Lemaitre who will start for the Breton club. Having seen an uptick in form and performances, Franck Haise is expected to persist with a back three as he heads down south to face his former club. title: Lille predicted XI v Lens: Davide Ancelotti to start with a false No.9? - Yahoo Sports
content: Lille OSC may start the Derby du Nord against RC Lens without a recognised centre-forward. Olivier Giroud may be left on the bench, whilst Ayase Ueda is currently injured. Giroud has rarely started for Lille this season, and even despite Ueda's absence on Friday night, he may not be included in Davide Ancelotti's XI. Instead, it may be Hakon Arnar Haraldsson who starts, potentially as a false No.9. There is also the absence of Tanguy Nianzou to contend with, whilst the likes of Tiago Santos and Hamza Igamane are more long-term absentees. Both are recovering from ACL injuries. Dilane Bakwa, currently on loan from Nottingham Forest, may also have to settle for a place on the bench. Ethan Mbappé is expected to continue on the right, whilst academy product Soriba Diaoune may be rewarded for his recent form with a place on the left of the attack. Berke Ozer; Romain Perraud, Alexsandro, Nathan Ngoy, Maxima Goffi; Benjamin André, Nabil Bentaleb, Ngal'ayel Mukau; Soriba Diaoune, Hakon Arnar Haraldsson, Ethan Mbappé. (L'Éq)

title: Lens predicted XI v Lille: Jean-Clair Todibo to start, Ismaelo Ganiou out - Yahoo Sports
content: RC Lens are without key players at both ends of the pitch as they prepare to make the short trip to face fierce rivals Lille OSC on Friday night. Ismaelo Ganiou recently underwent minor surgery and is expected to be out for several weeks. He is a big miss at the back, especially as Maik Nawrocki, brought in to provide cover at the back over the summer, is expected to miss much of the season with an ACL injury. Jean-Clair Todibo has struggled since joining Lens on loan from West Ham United, however, he is expected to start tonight. There are also absences up front. Abdalllah Sima is out until the other side of the international break, whilst Odsonne Édouard is the latest to succumb to an injury that will rule him out for several weeks, perhaps until 2027. Robin Risser; Jean-Clair Todibo, Samson Baidoo, Jonathan Gradit; Matthieu Udol, Amadou Haidara, Michael Cuisance, Ruben Aguilar; Florian Sotoca, Thorgan Hazard, Florian Thauvin. (L'Éq)

title: Commonwealth v. Javier B. Walker - City of Norfolk (.gov)
content: NORFOLK, Va. — Javier Braxton Walker, 28, was sentenced on Oct. 2 to serve five years in prison after he pleaded guilty in June to 12 counts of possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM; known under Virginia law as “child pornography”), a crime which police investigated following a cyber tip they received earlier this year. On Jan. 5, 2026, SpaceXAI — the company behind the “Grok” artificial intelligence chatbot available on the social media platform known as “X” — reported to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) that one of its users, later identified as Mr. Walker, uploaded 21 known images of CSAM to the website. “Known images” refers to CSAM that have already been reported to NCMEC and have been assigned digital fingerprints, known as “hash values,” that allow NCMEC to more easily identify new uploads of the same content. Following the cyber tip, NCMEC investigators located Mr. Walker’s Internet protocol address, a unique identifier that internet service providers assign to routers or computers of end users, in Norfolk and referred the case to the Norfolk Police Department. Detectives then identified Mr. Walker based on the information associated with his IP address, and the police arrested Mr. Walker in March. After being advised of his Miranda rights, Mr. Walker admitted to having uploaded CSAM and other images to Grok and having prompted the chatbot to produce new or manipulated CSAM based on those images. On June 30, Mr. Walker entered an agreement to plead guilty to one count of possessing child pornography as well as 11 counts of subsequent-offense possession of child pornography and to face an active sentence of up to 10 years in prison, which is within Mr. Walker’s sentencing guidelines range. Judge Robert B. Rigney accepted Mr. Walker’s plea agreement and continued his case for the preparation of a pre-sentence report and a sentencing hearing on Oct. 2. After hearing sentencing arguments from the Commonwealth and Mr. Walker’s defense counsel, Judge Rigney sentenced Mr. Walker to serve five years in prison with six months of post-release supervision on the first count of possessing CSAM and suspended another 11 years in prison for the 11 remaining charges on the conditions that Mr. Walker completes two years of supervised probation and three years of uniform good behavior following his release from prison. Mr. Walker will also be required to register as a sex offender and complete any related treatments as recommended by probation. “Child sexual abuse material depicts children suffering sexual abuse. Acquiring and sharing this material is like opening Pandora’s Box; the victim of this crime will have to live with the knowledge that the images of his or her abuse will almost certainly live on forever,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Ramin Fatehi. “The use of AI chatbots to create further CSAM using the originals as templates only makes things worse. Fortunately, the Virginia General Assembly has made AI-generated CSAM just as illegal as live CSAM. Our duty to protect children from abusers and potential abusers demands a serious response like the sentence that Mr. Walker will now serve.” Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney J. Drew Fairbanks prosecuted Mr. Walker’s case, and Norfolk Police Detectives Vanna S. Scholefield-Burke and Robert L. Miller led the investigation.

title: Commonwealth v. Trevonte G. Dugue - City of Norfolk (.gov)
content: NORFOLK, Va. — A jury convicted Trevonte Gerard Dugue, 30, on Wednesday of second-degree murder and using a firearm in the commission of murder after he shot and killed 27-year-old Tyrone Jontrell Walker Jr. outside an Ocean View convenience store in 2025. On the night of Nov. 25, 2025, Mr. Dugue and Mr. Walker — who were not known to be acquainted and had arrived separately — were among many individuals interacting outside of a convenience store at 123 W. Ocean View Ave. Security footage from the outside of the store showed Mr. Dugue having a brief conversation with the victim, who was not armed, before Mr. Dugue pointed a firearm at the victim and shot him in his face. The victim collapsed, Mr. Dugue turned to run away, and someone else (whose identity is unknown) shot Mr. Dugue in his torso. Witnesses rendered aid to the victim before police and medics arrived, and Mr. Dugue was picked up by an individual who drove him to a different convenience store where someone called 911 to report that Mr. Dugue had been shot. Meanwhile, medics transported the victim to a hospital, where he was admitted to intensive care and treated but was pronounced brain-dead and succumbed to his injury on Nov. 28. After responding to the report of Mr. Dugue’s gunshot wound, Norfolk Police were able to connect the two shootings, get Mr. Dugue to a hospital for treatment, and detain Mr. Dugue as a suspect in Mr. Walker’s murder after he was released from the hospital. Mr. Dugue agreed to speak with detectives and identified himself in photos pulled from the security camera footage. After confirming Mr. Dugue’s identity, the police charged Mr. Dugue with second-degree murder and using a firearm in the commission of murder. After reviewing Mr. Dugue’s case, the Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office secured a direct indictment from a grand jury against Mr. Dugue for first-degree murder. The investigation into who shot Mr. Dugue remains ongoing. Mr. Dugue pleaded not guilty to his charges and opted to be tried by a jury. After hearing the evidence and arguments between Oct. 26 and 28, 2026, and deliberating for nearly three hours, the jury found Mr. Dugue guilty of second-degree murder and using a firearm in the commission of murder. Judge Tasha D. Scott, who presided over the trial, set Mr. Dugue’s sentencing hearing on Jan. 15, 2027. “Mr. Dugue shot the victim with no provocation and no excuse, committing a true act of senseless violence,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Ramin Fatehi. “My condolences go to Mr. Walker’s family, who continue to grieve the loss of their loved one, and my appreciation goes to the eyewitnesses and good Samaritans who helped solve this case and to the businesses whose camera systems told a clear and unbiased story. My colleagues and I will continue to seek accountability for the people who kill in our city.” Senior Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney Liane Galardi and Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney Jessica L. Terkovich are prosecuting Mr. Dugue’s case, and Norfolk Police Detective Kyle D. Austin led the investigation.

title: New Instadoc Goes Inside the Jane Doe v. Cornell Case - Netflix
content:
The explosive lawsuit brought by Jane Doe — the former Cornell University student who alleges she was drugged and raped at the school’s Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024 — has sparked widespread protests and a fervent national debate about how colleges and universities handle sexual assault. Now, a new installment of Instadocs travels to the center of that fallout as the story continues to unfold. Here’s everything to know about Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell, which is now streaming on Netflix. With firsthand accounts from the editors of the student newspaper The Cornell Daily Sun, other Cornell students, New York Governor Kathy Hochul, and Jane Doe’s attorney, the newest installment of the documentary series examines the often flawed systems that investigate students’ claims of sexual assault. These include campus police and Title IX, the process at most US universities for reporting and investigating accusations of sexual misconduct. Generations of students have turned to these systems for protection and due process. Jane Doe tried both, and the outcry over her case has pressed the question: Are the systems delivering on their promise? The documentary premiered on Oct. 29, 2026. It’s now streaming. Jane Doe v. Cornell. Cornell Daily Sun senior editor Cereese Qusba, left, and Sophia Dasser, editor in chief, take notes during the student assembly on sexual violence held at Cornell University amid the Chi Phi lawsuit. Instadocs is Netflix’s quick-turn documentary series that moves at the speed of the story and arrives at the height of the conversation. Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell is the fifth installment in the series, following Alex Murdaugh, Unconvicted, The Prediction Games, The Decoy Plane, and AI Gone Wild, all available to stream now. Learn more about the series here. Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell is produced by Words + Pictures. Steve Yaccino serves as showrunner. Executive producers are Josh Tyrangiel, Connor Schell, Yaccino, Libby Geist, Aaron Cohen, and Alexa Conway, with supervising producers Amel Guettatfi and Rakhee Jethwa. Instadocs goes inside the rape investigation and Jane Doe lawsuit at Cornell University, with the student journalists at the forefront of the story.
